emi.intro: An ₹8,00,000 car loan at 9% over sixty months — the sort of quote a dealership prints on a single page and asks you to sign.

impval.intro: An investor offers ₹10 lakh for 10% of the company. The cheque and the stake are two views of one price; divide the first by the second and the sentence turns into a ₹1 crore valuation of the whole business.
impval.outro: ₹10 lakh for 10% prices the company at ₹1 crore - those are the two fields above. Ask for the same ₹10 lakh at 20% instead and the implied price drops to ₹50 lakh; change either field and the whole-company number follows.
impval.hi_intro: Ek investor ₹10 lakh de raha hai company ke 10% ke liye. Cheque aur stake ek hi price ke do roop hain; pehle ko doosre se divide karo aur sentence poore business ka ₹1 crore valuation ban jaata hai.
impval.hi_outro: ₹10 lakh for 10% company ko ₹1 crore par rakhta hai - upar wahi do field hain. Wahi ₹10 lakh 20% ke liye maango to implied price ₹50 lakh par aa jaata hai; koi bhi field badlo aur poore company ka number saath chalta hai.

prepost.intro: A term sheet names a ₹90,00,000 pre-money and a ₹10,00,000 cheque. Neither number says what the investor ends up owning; add them for the post-money, and measure the stake against that total.
prepost.outro: ₹10,00,000 on a ₹90,00,000 pre-money makes a ₹1,00,00,000 company and hands over 10%. Hold the pre-money and raise the cheque and the stake rises with it; change either field to watch the split move.

prepost.hi_outro: ₹90,00,000 pre-money par ₹10,00,000 ka cheque ₹1,00,00,000 company banata hai aur 10% de deta hai. Pre-money jaga par rakho aur cheque badhao to stake bhi badhta hai; split hilta dekhne ke liye koi bhi field badlo.
